sections.context: The GitHub implementation in internal/forge/github/repo.go uses Git.GetRef to get main's SHA, then Git.CreateRef to create the new branch. issues.title: Implement Gitea CreateOrUpdateFile via API

sections.summary: Replace the ErrNotImplemented stub for CreateOrUpdateFile in internal/forge/gitea/gitea.go with a working implementation.
sections.context: The GitHub implementation checks if the file exists (to get its SHA for updates), then calls Repositories.CreateFile. The Gitea SDK has CreateFile(owner, repo, path, CreateFileOptions) and UpdateFile(owner, repo, path, UpdateFileOptions). The Gitea API requires the file's existing SHA for updates (same as GitHub). Use GetContents to check existence first, then branch to create vs update. The CreateFileOptions needs BranchName, Content (base64), and NewBranchName (optional). Content must be base64-encoded for the Gitea API.

issues.title: Implement Gitea GetPRChecks and ListReviewComments via SDK

sections.summary: Replace ErrNotImplemented stubs for GetPRChecks and ListReviewComments in internal/forge/gitea/gitea.go.
sections.context:
GetPRChecks: Gitea's commit status API is GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/statuses. The PR watcher uses GetPRChecks to verify CI passed before auto-merging. Map Gitea's CommitStatus to forge.Check{Name, Status}. Gitea status states: pending, success, error, failure — map to forge.CheckStatus enum.

ListReviewComments: Gitea's PR review API is GET /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews, then GET reviews/{id}/comments for individual review comments. Map to forge.ReviewComment{Author, Body, Path, StartLine, EndLine, Resolved, CreatedAt}. This is used by the QC agent to read review feedback.

Note: If Gitea's API doesn't directly support line-level review comments in a single call, document the limitation and implement the best available approximation.

issues.title: Implement Gitea RepoReader interface (ListFiles, ReadFile, GetDiff, ListBranches, GetCommitLog, SearchCode)

sections.summary: Implement all six RepoReader methods for the Gitea adapter and add the compile-time interface check.
sections.context:
The GitHub implementation is in internal/forge/github/repo.go — use it as the reference for field mapping. The Gitea SDK equivalents:

- ListFiles → GetContents(owner, repo, path, ref) returns []*ContentsResponse
- ReadFile → GetContents(owner, repo, path, ref) returns *ContentsResponse with Content field (base64)
- GetDiff → GetRepoCompare(owner, repo, base...head) or use raw diff endpoint
- ListBranches → ListRepoBranches(owner, repo, ListRepoBranchesOptions)
- GetCommitLog → ListRepoCommits(owner, repo, ListRepoCommitsOption{SHA: branch})
- SearchCode → Gitea API: GET /api/v1/repos/search?q=... (limited vs GitHub). If Gitea lacks repo-scoped code search, implement as a grep-over-tree fallback or return ErrNotImplemented with a clear comment explaining why.

Add `var _ forge.RepoReader = (*Client)(nil)` compile-time check at the top of the file alongside the existing IssueTracker and RepoWriter checks.

These methods are used by MCP tools (tools_repo.go) for the check-in agent to browse code, read files, and inspect branches.
acceptance_criteria: All six RepoReader methods implemented with Gitea SDK calls
Compile-time check var _ forge.RepoReader = (*Client)(nil) added
Content decoding handles base64 (Gitea returns base64-encoded file content)

issues.title: Research Gitea Actions runner configuration and workflow compatibility with GitHub Actions

sections.summary: Document what is needed to run the existing GitHub Actions workflows on Gitea Actions, identifying compatibility gaps and required changes.
sections.context:
The repo has 6 workflows:
- ci.yml: go build, test, lint (golangci-lint), markdownlint, SPA build
- codeql.yml: GitHub CodeQL security scanning
- nightly.yml: scheduled tasks
- release-gate.yml: pre-release checks
- release-please.yml: automated release management
- copilot-setup-steps.yml: Copilot agent setup

Gitea Actions is based on act (nektos/act) and supports most GitHub Actions syntax. Key questions:
1. Which workflows can run unmodified on Gitea Actions?
2. Which require changes (e.g., different action references, missing marketplace actions)?
3. Is CodeQL available on Gitea Actions, or does it need an alternative (e.g., gosec, govulncheck)?
4. Does release-please have a Gitea-compatible mode?
5. What runner type is needed (Docker, host, LXC)?
6. Can the Gitea Actions runner on CT 200 handle Go builds (memory, disk, Go toolchain)?
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix: each of the 6 workflows rated as compatible/needs-changes/not-portable
For each 'needs-changes' workflow, specific changes documented
Runner requirements documented (CPU, memory, disk, installed tools)
Alternative tools identified for any GitHub-only features (CodeQL, release-please)
Recommendation on runner deployment: Docker container vs host process on CT 200

Alternatively, add --forge both to create on both forges sequentially.

issues.title: Build issue migration script: GitHub → Gitea

sections.summary: Create a script that exports open issues from GitHub and imports them into the Gitea repo, preserving frontmatter, labels, and comments.
sections.context:
Open issues on GitHub need to exist on Gitea for the dispatcher to work against both forges. The script should:
1. Use `gh` CLI to export open issues from HerbHall/samverk (JSON format)
2. For each issue, resolve label names to Gitea integer IDs
3. Create the issue on Gitea via API, preserving title, body (with YAML frontmatter), and labels
4. Migrate comments (in order) for each issue
5. Log a mapping table: GitHub issue # → Gitea issue # (numbers will differ)
6. Update depends_on references in frontmatter to use Gitea issue numbers

Note: Issue numbers WILL differ between forges. The depends_on fields in frontmatter reference issue numbers, so the script needs a second pass to update cross-references. This is the trickiest part.

Output: scripts/migrate-issues.sh (or .py if Python makes the JSON handling easier).
acceptance_criteria: Script exports all open issues from GitHub with body, labels, and comments

issues.title: Write ADR-031: Dual-Forge Operational Model

sections.summary: Document the decision to run Samverk in dual-forge mode (GitHub + Gitea) with the operational model, trade-offs, and sync strategy.
sections.context:
ADR-013 established the forge abstraction. ADR-019 established self-hosted-first. ADR-023 defined per-project repos. This ADR captures the operational decision:
- Why dual-forge (dogfooding Gitea adapter, self-hosted sovereignty, GitHub for public visibility)
- How code sync works (dual-push remote)
- How issue sync works (migration script, or independent issue sets per forge)
- How the dispatcher handles both (dual project entries in server.yaml)
- What happens when issues diverge between forges
- Trade-offs: operational complexity vs. forge independence validation

Follow the existing ADR format in docs/decisions/.

issues.title: End-to-end validation: full agent loop on Gitea (create issue → agent executes → PR merged → issue closed)

sections.summary: Complete end-to-end validation of the Samverk agent loop running entirely on Gitea: from issue creation through agent execution, PR creation, CI validation, PR merge, and issue closure.
sections.context:
This is the final gate before declaring the Gitea migration operational. The full loop:
1. Create a real task issue on Gitea with proper frontmatter and labels
2. Dispatcher (running on CT 202) picks up the issue from Gitea
3. Agent runner claims the issue, creates a branch on Gitea
4. Agent writes code/changes to the branch via Gitea adapter
5. Agent opens a PR on Gitea
6. Gitea Actions CI runs on the PR
7. PR watcher detects passing CI via GetPRChecks
8. PR watcher auto-merges the PR via MergePullRequest
9. Issue transitions to status:done

Every step must work against Gitea, not GitHub. This validates the entire forge abstraction layer end-to-end.

Document results as a timestamped runbook with pass/fail for each step.
acceptance_criteria: Issue created on Gitea with correct frontmatter and labels
Dispatcher picks up issue within one poll cycle
Agent creates branch on Gitea repo
Agent writes file(s) to branch via Gitea CreateOrUpdateFile
Agent opens PR on Gitea via CreatePullRequest
Gitea Actions CI runs and passes on the PR
PR watcher reads CI status via GetPRChecks
PR watcher auto-merges via MergePullRequest
Issue reaches status:done
Timestamped runbook documenting each step's result

issues.title: End-to-end validation: conversational check-in via MCP against dual-forge

sections.summary: Final human validation: open a Claude session, connect to Samverk MCP, and perform a complete check-in workflow spanning both GitHub and Gitea projects.
sections.context:
The product promise from ADR-011: 'You open a chat on any device and ask how's my project doing.' This test validates that promise works with dual-forge.

1. Open Claude (Desktop, mobile, or claude.ai)
2. Connect to Samverk MCP
3. Ask 'how's samverk doing?' — should aggregate data from both forges
4. Create an issue via conversation — should appear on the configured forge
5. Switch projects between GitHub and Gitea variants
6. Review the digest — should show status from both

This is the 'it works from my phone' test. If this passes, the Gitea migration is operational.
acceptance_criteria: Conversational check-in returns status from both GitHub and Gitea
Issue creation via MCP succeeds on both forges
Project switching works seamlessly
Digest aggregates data from dual-forge configuration
Workflow tested from at least two devices (desktop + mobile)
Migration declared operational
